questions.q: Explain why encryption protects data that has already been stolen.

markPoints.concept: the data is scrambled and cannot be read without the key
markPoints.exemplar: The stolen data is scrambled and cannot be read without the key.

markPoints.concept: so it is of no use to whoever took it
accept: no use|useless|worthless|cannot use|no value|cannot do anything|tells them nothing|pointless|no good|means nothing|cannot read it
markPoints.exemplar: So it is of no use to whoever took it.

questions.example: Encrypted data is scrambled into a form that cannot be read without the key, so even though the attacker has the file, what they have is meaningless and of no use to them.
questions.paraphrase: Because the information has been turned into something unreadable without the key, the thief ends up with a file that tells them nothing.
questions.feedback: Encryption does not stop theft; it makes the theft worthless.
questions.misconception: A common wrong answer is that encryption stops data being stolen. It does not.
